# sv0-flipper-ble-scanner: embedded consumer — toolchain enablement hub

## purpose

A Flipper Zero (STM32WB55, `f7`) BLE **observer** app whose product logic
(advertising-data parsing, device table, dedup, filters, scanner state) is
written in sv0. It is shipped as generated C plus a minimal C bridge inside a
`.fap` (preferred R1 path A), or as an internal app in custom firmware
(preview path B).

The governing document is:

- `~/Documents/project-specs/sv0-flipper-ble-scanner/SPEC.md`: version
  `0.2.1` (0.2.0 plus the 2026-09-27 CLI reconciliation and OQ resolutions), sv0 audit 2026-08-31 (meta `05587fc`, sv0c `cab4ca1`), Flipper
  audit 2026-08-23. OQ-001/002/008/009 (the sv0-side decisions) resolved 2026-09-27; OQ-003..007 belong to the Flipper/product side.

The sibling `~/Documents/project-specs/c-flipper-ble-scanner/SPEC.md` is an
independent **native C** implementation of the same product. It carries no
sv0 toolchain obligations and is out of scope here.

This hub owns only the **toolchain side**: the non-hosted emission, embedded
runtime, ABI, and regression evidence the scanner's F0 gate needs from sv0.
Radio, firmware, and UI work belongs to the future scanner repo. The project
is SPEC-governed and **not** a toolchain milestone (absent from
`task/milestone-orientation.json`). Its freestanding asks are the first
concrete consumer for design milestone 6 (`task/sv0-toolchain-milestone-6-kernel.Rmd`).

## what the scanner needs from the toolchain (SPEC §4.4, §15, Appendix B)

| Need | SPEC | State now (2026-09-27) |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical, hash-stable `--emit=c` for a project | TOOL-002, E-009 | **Ready** (atomic `--emit=c -o`). The spelling changes under the installed-toolchain spec (X-1). |
| Non-hosted entry: no hosted `main(argc, argv)`/`sv0_runtime_init`; a library or FAP entry | TOOL-003, TOOL-005, E-011, OQ-001 | **Missing.** Hosted entry ABI v1 always emits `sv0_user_main` + C `main`. |
| Freestanding runtime: no stdio, `exit`, getenv, filesystem, or bootstrap pools | RT-001..003, RT-008..010, E-004, OQ-002 | **Missing.** `sv0_runtime.h` is hosted. Its tables are process-global (now growable, sv0c `5dce60e`, but still malloc-backed and never released). |
| Namespaced generated symbols | RT-006 | **Partial.** User identifiers are prefixed `sv0u_` (sv0c `d6e306d`). A collision audit against firmware + the hosted ABI names is still needed. |
| C → sv0 calls and callback-shaped invocation | E-001..003, §15.1 | **Partial.** C can call generated `sv0u_*` functions, but there is no stable exported-symbol contract (`#[export_c]`-style) or naming guarantee. |
| sv0 → C calls (bridge, Furi) | OQ-008 | **Partial.** `#[extern_c]` imports ship on the C backend (FFI v1). This answers OQ-008's "motivates an sv0 `extern` feature" question: the feature exists. What is missing is struct/pointer ABI layout (shared with GUI-U03). |
| ABI width/sign/align/offset assertions | RT-005, E-001, E-002 | **Missing** (shared with GUI-U03). |
| Contract failure → recoverable stop, not `exit(1)` | RT-002, E-005 | **Missing.** Contract failure is `exit(1)` from inline header helpers. |
| C/VM pure-core parity; dev + release; ASan/UBSan | TOOL-007, TOOL-008, E-010 | **Ready** (behavioral parity harness, release parity, sanitizer corpus). |
| Regression pack for scanner-used shapes | TOOL-010, E-012 | Scanner-repo work over existing corpora. |

## cross-spec conflict

| # | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| X-1 | The scanner spec standardizes `sv0c --emit=c --project <dir> -o …` and host policy (profile, contract mode, retained C, cc) in `sv0.toml`. The installed-toolchain spec rejects `--project` in installed `sv0c` and forbids policy keys in manifest v1. | Amend the scanner spec: `sv0c --emit=c -o <path> <dir>` with a v1 manifest; host policy on the command line; embedded settings in the separate integration manifest the scanner spec already requires (§15.3). Until the TID R0 CLI lands, the repo-driver adapter keeps `--project` working. **Resolved 2026-09-27:** written into the scanner spec `0.2.1`. |

## sequencing

FLP-U01 is a decision and can happen any time. FLP-U02..U05 are real compiler
and runtime work with no consumer repo yet. Schedule them together with M6
phase 2 ("freestanding linking model"), or earlier if the scanner repo starts.
They do not block M5 or TID.
